newsitem.title: UK: WWF wants action to save sharks from extinction.
newsitem.headline: WWF wants action to save sharks from extinction.

text.p: The World Wide Fund for Nature (WWF) called on Thursday for tighter international management and monitoring of shark fishing order to save the shark population from extinction.
It said in a study that few, if any, controls existed to regulate shark fishing, and said demand for shark meat, fins, skin and internal organs was burgeoning.

"WWF is calling for immediate action to save shark populations all over the world from commercial and perhaps even biological extinction," Michael Sutton, the director of WWF's Endangered Seas Campaign, said in a statement with the study.
"There is absolutely no management on an international basis for sharks anywhere in the world and very few countries control shark fisheries in their own waters," he added.
WWF said various types of shark now featured regularly in the diets of Europeans, although food outlets sometimes went out of their way to obscure the fact.
It estimated that 30 percent of fish and chip shops in southern Britain offered a type of shark known as piked or spiny dogfish, but it was generally sold as "rock salmon".
According to the United Nations' Food and Agriculture Organisation (FAO) the total world shark catch reached 730,784 tonnes in 1994.

But WWF said the true catch was much higher. Many low-value sharks were caught but discarded at sea, either whole or with the fins removed, while some countries, such as China, which has a growing fleet, did not report volumes.
